tasks.subject: Task 1: Fix the deckpile overlapping content on mobile
tasks.description:
**Goal:** .deckpile never overlaps the pack-selection text or other flow content at <=560px.

**Files:** Modify ui/shared.css:614-617

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- .tabletop reserves enough bottom padding at <=560px to clear .deckpile's full footprint
- Desktop (>560px) unaffected

**Verify:** rebuild docs/draft.html, screenshot at 375x812, confirm no overlap.

See plans/2026-09-22-mobile-coverflow-draft-plan.md Task 1 for exact diff.

tasks.subject: Task 2: Coverflow CSS foundation
tasks.description:
**Goal:** CSS for .hand.coverflow / .cftrack / depth classes / group label / touch handling exists, inert until wired.

**Files:** Modify ui/shared.css (after line 440; and line 658 touch-action rule)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- .hand.coverflow lays out a label above a snap-scrolling track
- .dcard has .focused / .near / neither depth states
- .cftrack .dcard gets touch-action:pan-x alongside the existing fan rule

**Verify:** grep -c "cftrack" ui/shared.css >= 5; python3 test_suite.py all green.

See plans/2026-09-22-mobile-coverflow-draft-plan.md Task 2 for exact CSS.

tasks.subject: Task 3: Coverflow for Pack 1 Pick 1
tasks.description:
**Goal:** On mobile, p1DrawHand() renders the pack as a coverflow instead of a fan; swipe-up-to-pick keeps working unchanged; colour-sort groups show as a label above the focused card.

**Files:** Modify ui/cube.js:696-758 (p1DrawHand), ui/cube.js:1024-1029 (p1LayoutHand), new function p1WireCoverflow(track, groups) above p1LayoutHand.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- <=560px renders .hand.coverflow with flat .cftrack cards, no .handgroup boxing even when colour-sorted
- >560px behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged (fan, grouped runs, p1LayoutHand sizing)
- Horizontal swipe browses; centered card full-size, neighbours smaller
- Swipe-up on focused card still picks it via unmodified p1Swipe/p1Take
- Colour sort shows/updates a group label above the focused card
- p1LayoutHand is a no-op when #p1Hand has class coverflow

**Verify:** python3 test_suite.py all green; live browser-pane check at 375x812 (open pack, browse, swipe-pick, colour sort label) and at desktop width (fan unchanged).

See plans/2026-09-22-mobile-coverflow-draft-plan.md Task 3 for exact diffs and full p1WireCoverflow code.

tasks.subject: Task 4: Coverflow for the signal drill
tasks.description:
**Goal:** On mobile, the drill's main pack pile (d.left) renders as a browse-only coverflow; after-answer reveal pile and everything else in the drill unchanged.

**Files:** Modify ui/cube.js:1591-1592 and the wiring block right after box.innerHTML in p1DrillView (~line 1615-1619).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- <=560px: d.left renders as .hand.coverflow, no group label, no pick gesture
- >560px: unchanged (.stacks > .stack > .pile)
- d.taken pile unaffected at any width
- Tapping a coverflow card still opens zoom preview only

**Verify:** python3 test_suite.py all green; live check at 375x812 (drill pack browses, tap zooms, no swipe-pick affordance) and desktop (unchanged stacked pile).

See plans/2026-09-22-mobile-coverflow-draft-plan.md Task 4 for exact diff.

tasks.subject: Task 5: Regression checks
tasks.description:
**Goal:** test_suite.py locks in the coverflow markup/CSS/wiring added in Tasks 1-4, matching the existing grep-style convention.

**Files:** Modify test_suite.py, new function test_mobile_coverflow() called from main() after test_signal_drill().

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Checks confirm coverflow CSS exists (.hand.coverflow, .cftrack, depth classes, deckpile padding-bottom)
- Checks confirm p1DrawHand's mobile branch and matchMedia usage
- Checks confirm p1WireCoverflow exists and is called from both p1DrawHand and p1DrillView
- Checks confirm p1LayoutHand bails early for coverflow
- python3 test_suite.py reports all green including new checks

**Verify:** python3 test_suite.py all green; temporarily break one check to confirm it can fail, then revert.

See plans/2026-09-22-mobile-coverflow-draft-plan.md Task 5 for the full test function.
